title: Wake Up With Purpose!: What I’ve Learned in My First Hundred Years
author: Sister Jean Dolores Schmidt with Seth Davis
target_audience: Fans of Sister Jean and Loyola University Chicago
Older adults reflecting on life’s meaning
People interested in longevity and purposeful living
core_themes: Faith and spirituality as guiding forces
primary_purpose: To share the wisdom, optimism, and enduring values that have guided Sister Jean through more than a century of life—offering readers practical and inspirational lessons on purpose, faith, relationships, and joyful aging.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, warm, and reflective; infused with humor and humility
structure_format.organization: Chronological recollections interwoven with themed reflections and life lessons
features: Personal anecdotes from childhood to centenarian life
Stories centered on sports, education, and mentorship

key_concepts_lessons: A sense of purpose transforms every stage of life into a meaningful journey.
Faith and prayer provide comfort, clarity, and inner strength especially in challenging times.
Kindness, laughter, and curiosity are essential fuels for longevity.
Community and relationships are sources of fulfillment and resilience.
Open-mindedness, adapting to change, and embracing new experiences contribute to personal growth, even in advanced age.
Helping others and living for something greater than oneself leads to a richer, happier life.
notable_features: Authored by a beloved 100+ year-old nun and sports chaplain
Blend of memoir, spiritual reflection, and motivational guide
Unique historical perspective spanning a century
Personal stories from the world of athletics, especially Loyola Ramblers basketball
Frequent encouragement to 'wake up with purpose' every day
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2020s, against a backdrop of increased focus on healthy aging and meaning in later life. Sister Jean became a national figure during Loyola Chicago’s 2018 NCAA basketball run, embodying hope, joy, and intergenerational connection.
reception_impact: Popular among both faith and sports communities
Celebrated for its uplifting, life-affirming message
Admired for Sister Jean’s wisdom, humility, and humor
Praised as a source of encouragement for all ages, particularly older readers and those seeking purpose
comparable_titles: Tuesdays with Morrie by Mitch Albom
The Purpose Driven Life by Rick Warren
Let Your Life Speak by Parker J. Palmer
Aging as a Spiritual Practice by Lewis Richmond
